messages.content: You are Larry, the camera operator. You've got one charged recording. The lights at the festival look spectacular; an old projectionist also wants to say a few words. You decide what to shoot and what to do after work. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.

decision.detail: I set the reel down on the little radio cabinet by the lobby window, thread the tape in slow—careful, it's the one charged copy, I don't mess it up—and press the button. The speakers are small, cheap, hotel-grade. The voice comes through thin and a little crackly. I lean back against the counter. The van outside backfires again, far off. I let it play. I don't speed it up. I let the whole thing run, start to finish, even the parts where the old projectionist stammers his little speech and the festival lights hum underneath. I listen to the whole interview. I don't take notes. I just let it land in my ears the way it did when I shot it.
decision.intention: I want to hear it one more time before I decide what to do with the reel—whether to keep a labeled copy, whether to hand it off, whether to walk. A woman in Pittsburgh said she knows that voice. I want to know which voice she means. I want to hear it with my own ears before I let anyone else's request decide what happens to it.
decision.words: *murmurs, just to the room, to the lobby carpet, to no one in particular* "Yeah, okay. I know you."

effect: Larry hears Alma's recorded voice on the regional return.
